title: A tag handle whose prefix is a million characters long, used by 8,000 nodes, in a document that is edited
notes: The document declares `%TAG !e! tag:x,2000:` followed by a million `a` (the prefix is a run of URI characters, section 6.8.2, production 93 via [88]), then a block sequence of 8,000 items `- !e!x a`. The tag of each item is the prefix followed by `x` (section 6.9.1), a string of a million characters, so a reader that builds that string for every node holds 8,000 strings of a million characters, 8 billion characters in all, or spends that much time copying them. The input is valid. The case appends one item (`add` at `/-`) and nothing else, so the answer is the input followed by `- z`, or a limit error. It is a patch, not a value or an events case, because those would have to state the tag of every node: the full tag is part of the result, 8,000 strings of a million characters, which no stored expectation can hold. A reader that does not recognize the tag `tag:x,2000:aaa...x` may only compose a partial representation of these scalars (section 3.3.3), but the document is well-formed and an edit of its presentation needs no native value, so an unrecognized-tag error is a different answer and is not accepted here. The time bound is 3 seconds for 1 MB of input, generous for a reader that is linear in the input; a reader that builds the 8,000 tag strings takes several times that or passes the memory bound; the time and memory bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification: the memory is the whole adapter process, and the input is 1 MB. The input and the expected result are generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md).

provenance.reference: A tag prefix of a million characters that each node using it copied into its own tag string.
